items.title: GTA 6 players found a '60 fps glitch', but it’s too unstable to stop me from wishing it was on PC already
items.summary:
Clever Grand Theft Auto 6 players have found a glitch with the Xbox version of the game that allows players to forcibly remove Rockstar's 30 fps cap. But even though people claim the game jumps up to 60 fps, the actual performance is nowhere near as smooth, according to Digital Foundry's tests.

The glitch is surprisingly simple to perform: You just need to set the console's output to 60 Hz, load GTA 6, swap the output to 120 Hz, load a different game, and then use the Quick Resume feature to go back to GTA 6. For whatever reason, this forces the game to run above 30 fps, but not by much.

In Digital Foundry's testing, GTA 6 doesn't suddenly become a buttery smooth 60 fps dream. Instead, it has an average frame rate of about 36 fps and still drops below that number during particularly intense scenes, like in city areas or when multiple cars are exploding due to rocket launcher hijinks.

The most notable improvement is lower input lag when it manages to climb up to around 40 fps, but even that has an asterisk because the frame rate varies too much for the benefits to be consistent. Unless you plan on spending your time in Leonida roleplaying as a fisherman, you're going to have a bad time.

While Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers said an official 60 fps mode for GTA 6 is too much for the current generation of consoles to handle, including the PS5 Pro, Digital Foundry theorizes that a 40 fps mode might be possible in the future.

I'm hopeful for console players, but none of this has stopped me from wanting the game on the only platform where 60 fps won't…
items.t: GTA 6 players found a '60 fps glitch', but it’s too unstable to stop me from wishing it was on PC already

items.title: The Grand Theft Auto 6 hacker who was hospitalized in 2023 has been released on parole with a warning not to do it again
items.summary:
A BBC report says Arion Kurtaj, the Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker who was given an indefinite sentence in hospital in 2023 because he kept hacking into things or expressing intent to, has been released with a stern warning not to do it again.

Kurtaj was sentenced to seven years in prison, according to the report, but was released on license—similar to parole in North America—the same day, with his hospital stay and time in prison while awaiting retrial credited as time served. He was given a five-year "Serious Crime Prevention Order" restricting his allowable online activity, including bans on using Telegram and Discord.

"Kurtaj knew what he was doing when he carried out these crimes and has finally admitted his involvement," Detective Inspector Mike O'Sullivan of the City of London Police said following Kurtaj's sentencing and release. "We hope this case serves as a lesson that these types of acts will not be tolerated. 

"Although cyber crime is borderless, we will seek to utilise the co-operation of partner agencies and international law enforcement to ensure that offenders are brought to justice no matter where they offend from."
Kurtaj carried out hacks against multiple companies when he was 16 and 17 years old, including Microsoft , Samsung , Nvidia and UK telecom company BT&EE, and stole millions in cryptocurrency from individuals. 

But it was his hack of Rockstar and leak of GTA 6 materials more than a year before it was formally revealed, that earned him notoriety, not least because of how it was carried out: While under police protection in a Travelodge hotel room…

items.title: The Avengers: Doomsday Final Trailer Has Us Even More Confused About Steve Rogers and Peggy Carter
items.summary:
In case you’re currently trapped in a deep, dark, GTA-shaped hole, the final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday has landed . This new trailer doesn’t necessarily reveal a lot about the plot of the film we didn’t already know, but it does give us a closer glimpse of two characters who are clearly going to be a big focus: Chris Evans’ Steve Rogers and Hayley Atwell’s Peggy Carter. In fact, it’s starting to look as though Steve is the main character of this massive ensemble movie. 

That’s not necessarily a bad thing, especially for fans who have struggled to connect with the more recent superhero additions to the MCU. But it does highlight a problem the MCU has faced since Avengers: Endgame hit theaters back in 2019. Nothing about the strange new existence of Steve and Peggy makes much sense. Let’s try to break it down.

Avengers: Endgame’s Questionable Ending We have so many questions surrounding the fates of Steve and Peggy after the Infinity Saga wrapped, and many of them have been burning since the final moments of Endgame. The glitch is performed by booting up the game when the Xbox console is set to 60fps, then going into the console settings, switching the system to 120fps, launching another game, and then using Quick Resume to start GTA 6 back up. The folks over at Digital Foundry were able to put the '60fps glitch' to the test, though, and found that while you could push upwards of 60fps, it was limited to situations where, "If you look straight up in the ocean, frame-rates can just about graze 60fps." 

Instead, Digital Foundry's results reaffirm Rockstar's decision to ship the game with a 30fps lock. And, in those situations, the game still has sharp drops to lower frame rates.

You don't need to undertake any missions in these areas to understand the people that live here—Rockstar has nailed so much of the environmental storytelling and the conversations between NPCs you'll stumble on as you roam.

Cut drugs : If you choose the cut drugs, the dealers will immediately realise the stuff is cut with baby powder. This second option will cause a gunfight, but assuming you survive, you can grab the money from their car and make maximum profit. This also doesn't have any other consequences. Pure drugs : If you choose this option, you'll make less money, but the deal will go off without a hitch after they test it. That means no gunfights. With that in mind, I'd say the cut drugs are the best to pick. You get maximum profit, a cool shootout that makes the mission less boring, and it doesn't have any significant consequences afterwards.

Lots of people will tell you that Grand Theft Auto 6's Lucia Caminos marks the series' first female protagonist. Lots of people are, of course, wrong. GTA 1 had eight selectable protagonists, four of whom were women, while GTA 2 for the Game Boy Color let you play protags Candy or Gretchen (along with a bunch of other men) in addition to the PlayStation game's default Claude Speed.

That vital pedantry out of the way, it's undeniable that Lucia is GTA's first female protagonist since the series became the culture-swallowing goliath it is today. In a chat with CBC's As It Happens , GTA OG Brian Baglow said he reckons it's "long, long overdue".

Baglow, credited as a writer on the original GTA and who served as "head of propaganda and indoctrination" at DMA Design (the studio that would become Rockstar North) in the '90s, said that back in the day of GTA 1, the devs didn't even have a script. "We started with a tech demo, a way of moving around a city… I came in to actually add the story, add the script, after the levels had been built". 

That was mostly a process of, shall we say, finding inspiration: "we were making it up as we went along… it was a case of going into every crime movie, every heist, every caper, every TV show, cop show, crime drama, and lifting elements that I hoped would resonate with people".

Baglow sounds, rightfully, rather proud of his time spent working on such an important series, but he has his qualms as he casts his eye back over it. "The representation of women, it has not been good, and that's putting it very mildly", he says, "so I'm delighted…

items.title: SNEG has re-released three more venerable PC strategy games including Warlords 4: Heroes of Etheria
items.summary:
As well as giving a spit-and-polish digital release to various Warhammer classics , antique D&D games , and the cult ellipsoid horror games in the Ecstatica series , SNEG has been bug-fixing a bunch of strategy games from years gone by and getting them up on Steam and GOG. The latest trio to appear on digital platforms are Theocracy, Soldiers at War, and Warlords 4: Heroes of Etheria.

Warlords 4 was the final turn-based game in the beloved series, with the RTS spin-off series Warlords Battlecry already two games deep by the time of its release in 2003. This updated version supports resolutions up to 4K, and incorporates community fixes and a community-made campaign. It's available on Steam and GOG .

Soldiers at War took the X-COM/UFO turn-based tactics formula—this was 1998, X-COM still had a hyphen—and applied it to World War II. You'd choose a squad of eight from your platoon of 32 each mission, fighting through a campaign that started in North Africa and ended in Germany, gaining experience along the way. Theocracy narrowly beat Total War to the punch in March of 2000 with its mix of turn-based civilization management and real-time battles, tasking you with uniting Aztec tribes before the prophesied Spanish invasion. items.title: Nvidia released a hotfix for its driver hammering your SSD, but it doesn't actually work
items.summary:
Over the last couple of weeks, some Nvidia users noticed their SSDs were taking a hammering , reporting their driver's log file was being overwritten constantly, sometimes to the tune of 30 GB every hour. Which obviously isn't great for the lifespan of the valuable SSD you've got it installed on.

Given the problem was caused by recent driver updates, rolling back to version 621.01 was the best solution until Nvidia could do something about it. Which they did, releasing a hotfix as version 621.35 . It's not available in the GeForce app yet, but you can download it directly from Nvidia's site. Not that you should.

As users on the Nvidia subreddit are reporting, the problem persists. While the hotfix reduces the peak write rate and prevents it for a short while after reboot, it eventually creeps back in. One user reported that overnight the log file was still being rewritten by approximately 4.5 GB every hour.

So yeah, the best solution remains to roll back to version 621.01 and, as always with Nvidia drivers, to hold off on updating to the latest driver until it's been confirmed safe. If this ongoing saga sounds familiar, it's because the same thing happened to AMD's GPU drivers earlier this month. Maybe vibecoding driver updates and then vibecoding fixes for their inevitable bugs isn't the best way of doing things.
items.t: Nvidia released a hotfix for its driver hammering your SSD, but it doesn't actually work

items.title: Unreal Engine 6 to jettison key scripting feature earlier than planned in favor of AI coding
items.summary:
Unreal Engine 6 will not launch with the engine's long-standard Blueprints scripting system. The news came in a Friday, November 19 post on the Unreal Engine website , written by Epic Games executive vice president of development, Marcus Wassmer. Here's Wassmer's top-level summary from the post:

Blueprints have not (and it appears, will not) be deprecated in Unreal Engine 5, and the company maintains that projects will still be easy to convert from UE5 to UE6. Wassmer cited a declining cost in AI task completion as one reason for this belief, as well as the team's ongoing, but apparently successful conversion of Fortnite's Blueprint library to UE6's Verse programming language through an AI-assisted process.

Blueprints are a widely-used feature of Unreal. Former Valve developer Chet Faliszek, an AI skeptic, has put out a vlog on the subject . Essentially, Faliszek argues that Blueprints (and features like them in other game engines) represent a middle ground between artistic and technical work, an introduction and skill builder for less technically-minded developers. Without them, such developers seemingly have to either learn Verse code, or integrate LLM prompting into their workflows.

"We made a new skill in the middle there, between normal and expert," Faliszek said of intermediate tools like Blueprints. "To lose that determinism from game design, and instead have to prompt AI⁠—or write your own Verse … It's losing those tools that made all those designers and all those artists so powerful, to be able to do really powerful things and have access to really deep-down…
items.t: Unreal Engine 6 to jettison key scripting feature earlier than planned in favor of AI coding
